rationale: Correct the existing DSD Renewables record in place after a fresh GPT-5.6 Sol Pro review and independent source verification. DSD began as GE Solar in 2012, partnered with BlackRock and became the standalone DSD platform in 2019, and BlackRock acquired GE Renewable Energy's remaining interest in November 2020. Ares entered with $200 million of preferred equity in March 2022 and became majority owner following a 2025 consensual change-of-control and common-equity conversion. Cox Enterprises invested $250 million in November 2023. A July 2025 DSD proposal identifies Ares, BlackRock and Cox as the platform's current backers after the control transition. Add Cox as a current minority owner and GE Renewable Energy as the realized former owner, retain BlackRock as a current minority owner, and correct Ares to majority status. Exact current percentages are not publicly disclosed. The Global Renewable Power II vehicle is recorded as vehicle text because the repository has no matching Fund row. Global Infrastructure Partners is not a DSD owner merely because BlackRock acquired GIP. Sale exploration, restructuring and asset sales were reported, but no definitive signed platform sale, closing or later ownership transfer was identified through August 15, 2026.

companyFieldUpdates.description: DSD Renewables, legally Distributed Solar Development, LLC, is a Schenectady-based U.S. distributed-energy platform that develops, finances, acquires, owns and operates commercial, industrial, municipal and community solar, storage and EV-charging infrastructure. The business began as GE Solar in 2012 and became the standalone DSD platform in 2019 with backing from BlackRock's Global Renewable Power II strategy. BlackRock acquired GE Renewable Energy's remaining interest in November 2020. Ares Management invested $200 million through its Infrastructure and Power strategy in March 2022 and became majority owner after a 2025 change-of-control and common-equity conversion. Cox Enterprises made a $250 million minority strategic investment in November 2023. July 2025 DSD materials identify Ares, BlackRock and Cox as current platform backers; exact current percentages are not publicly disclosed. DSD reported $238 million of financing for 188 operating distributed-generation projects totaling 233 MW in August 2025. Individual projects, project SPVs, financing counterparties and the BlackRock/GIP manager combination are outside the canonical PortCo boundary. No signed or completed DSD platform sale was identified through August 15, 2026.
